result.means: each side was reasoned INDEPENDENTLY under OWL 2 RL and the entailed named ancestors were compared through the mapping itself. What this checks is the POSITION of the two terms in their hierarchies, not what they mean: a downgrade is a refutation (the subject sits under a mapped concept the object does not, or the reverse), and an upheld row means only that nothing this engine can see refutes it. Two siblings under one mapped parent have identical translated ancestors, so a row pairing the wrong sibling is upheld exactly as the right one is, which is why the predicate column never strengthens a claim. Only ancestors both sides can name are compared: an ancestor with no counterpart through the mapping is a coverage gap, named on the row and never counted as a disagreement, and a row with nothing comparable, including a term with no hierarchy at all, is not_refuted_nothing_compared and is NOT certified. A SKOS scheme's hierarchy is its skos:broader closure. It is NOT a proof: the comparison is over 29 of OWL 2 RL's 78 rules, and an axiom no rule fires on contributes to neither side. Run onto_dlp_boundary to see which of your axioms were invisible. No Lean checker has a theorem about SKOS match types, so nothing here is certified in this repository's sense of that word.
